How do I use CTEs (Common Table Expressions) and subqueries in HoneySQL?

HoneySQL supports both CTEs (WITH clauses) and subqueries for complex queries.

**Common Table Expressions (CTEs)**
```clojure
;; Basic CTE with :with
{:with [[:active_users {:select [:*]
                         :from [:users]
                         :where [:= :active true]}]]
 :select [:*]
 :from [:active_users]
 :where [:> :login_count 10]}
;; WITH active_users AS (SELECT * FROM users WHERE active = ?)
;; SELECT * FROM active_users WHERE login_count > ?

;; Multiple CTEs
{:with [[:recent_orders {:select [:*]
                          :from [:orders]
                          :where [:> :created_at #inst "2024-01-01"]}]
        [:high_value {:select [:*]
                      :from [:recent_orders]
                      :where [:> :total 1000]}]]
 :select [:user_id [:%count.* :order_count] [:%sum.total :total_spent]]
 :from [:high_value]
 :group-by [:user_id]}
```

**Recursive CTEs**
```clojure
;; Hierarchical data (org chart)
{:with-recursive [[:employee_hierarchy
                   {:union-all
                    [{:select [:id :name :manager_id [[:cast 1 :int] :level]]
                      :from [:employees]
                      :where [:is :manager_id nil]}  ; Root nodes
                     {:select [:e.id :e.name :e.manager_id [[:+ :eh.level 1] :level]]
                      :from [[:employees :e]]
                      :join [[:employee_hierarchy :eh] [:= :eh.id :e.manager_id]]}]}]]
 :select [:*]
 :from [:employee_hierarchy]
 :order-by [:level :name]}

;; Generates:
;; WITH RECURSIVE employee_hierarchy AS (
;;   SELECT id, name, manager_id, CAST(1 AS int) AS level
;;   FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL
;;   UNION ALL
;;   SELECT e.id, e.name, e.manager_id, eh.level + 1 AS level
;;   FROM employees AS e
;;   JOIN employee_hierarchy AS eh ON eh.id = e.manager_id
;; )
;; SELECT * FROM employee_hierarchy ORDER BY level, name
```

**Subqueries in SELECT**
```clojure
;; Scalar subquery
{:select [:u.*
          [{:select [[:%count.*]]
            :from [:orders]
            :where [:= :orders.user_id :u.id]} :order_count]]
 :from [[:users :u]]}
;; SELECT u.*, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE orders.user_id = u.id) AS order_count
;; FROM users AS u

;; Multiple scalar subqueries
{:select [:p.id :p.name
          [{:select [[:%avg.rating]]
            :from [:reviews]
            :where [:= :reviews.product_id :p.id]} :avg_rating]
          [{:select [[:%count.*]]
            :from [:order_items]
            :where [:= :order_items.product_id :p.id]} :times_ordered]]
 :from [[:products :p]]}
```

**Subqueries in FROM**
```clojure
;; Derived table
{:select [:top_users.*]
 :from [[{:select [:user_id [:%sum.total :total_spent]]
          :from [:orders]
          :group-by [:user_id]
          :having [:> :%sum.total 10000]} :top_users]]}

;; Join with subquery
{:select [:u.name :user_stats.order_count :user_stats.total_spent]
 :from [[:users :u]]
 :join [[{:select [:user_id
                   [:%count.* :order_count]
                   [:%sum.total :total_spent]]
          :from [:orders]
          :group-by [:user_id]} :user_stats]
        [:= :user_stats.user_id :u.id]]
 :order-by [[:user_stats.total_spent :desc]]}
```

**Subqueries in WHERE**
```clojure
;; IN with subquery
{:select [:*]
 :from [:products]
 :where [:in :category_id
         {:select [:id]
          :from [:categories]
          :where [:= :featured true]}]}
;; SELECT * FROM products WHERE category_id IN (SELECT id FROM categories WHERE featured = ?)

;; EXISTS
{:select [:*]
 :from [:users]
 :where [:exists {:select [1]
                  :from [:orders]
                  :where [:and
                          [:= :orders.user_id :users.id]
                          [:> :orders.total 100]]}]}
;; SELECT * FROM users WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders WHERE orders.user_id = users.id AND orders.total > ?)

;; NOT EXISTS
{:select [:*]
 :from [:products]
 :where [:not-exists {:select [1]
                      :from [:order_items]
                      :where [:= :order_items.product_id :products.id]}]}
;; Products never ordered

;; Comparison with subquery
{:select [:*]
 :from [:employees]
 :where [:> :salary {:select [[:%avg.salary]]
                     :from [:employees]}]}
;; Employees earning above average
```

**Complex CTE Example**
```clojure
(defn monthly-retention-report [ds year month]
  (jdbc/execute! ds
    (sql/format
      {:with [;; Users active in target month
              [:target_month_users
               {:select-distinct [:user_id]
                :from [:events]
                :where [:and
                        [:= [:extract :year :created_at] year]
                        [:= [:extract :month :created_at] month]]}]
              ;; Users active in previous month
              [:prev_month_users
               {:select-distinct [:user_id]
                :from [:events]
                :where [:and
                        [:= [:extract :year :created_at] (if (= month 1) (dec year) year)]
                        [:= [:extract :month :created_at] (if (= month 1) 12 (dec month))]]}]
              ;; Retained users (in both months)
              [:retained_users
               {:select [:t.user_id]
                :from [[:target_month_users :t]]
                :join [[:prev_month_users :p] [:= :t.user_id :p.user_id]]}]]
       :select [[:inline year] :year]
               [[:inline month] :month]
               [{:select [[:%count.*]] :from [:prev_month_users]} :prev_month_count]
               [{:select [[:%count.*]] :from [:target_month_users]} :current_month_count]
               [{:select [[:%count.*]] :from [:retained_users]} :retained_count]]})))
```

**Building CTEs Dynamically**
```clojure
(defn with-cte [query cte-name cte-query]
  (update query :with (fnil conj []) [cte-name cte-query]))

(defn build-analysis-query [filters]
  (-> {:select [:*] :from [:analysis_view]}
      (with-cte :filtered_data
        {:select [:*]
         :from [:raw_data]
         :where (build-where filters)})
      (with-cte :analysis_view
        {:select [:category [:%count.* :count] [:%avg.value :avg_value]]
         :from [:filtered_data]
         :group-by [:category]})))
```
How do I use INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and UPSERT in HoneySQL?

HoneySQL provides clean syntax for all data modification statements.

**INSERT**
```clojure
;; Single row with column-value map
(sql/format
  {:insert-into :users
   :values [{:name "Alice" :email "alice@example.com" :active true}]})
;; => ["INSERT INTO users (name, email, active) VALUES (?, ?, ?)" "Alice" "alice@example.com" true]

;; Multiple rows
(sql/format
  {:insert-into :users
   :values [{:name "Alice" :email "alice@example.com"}
            {:name "Bob" :email "bob@example.com"}
            {:name "Charlie" :email "charlie@example.com"}]})
;; INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES (?, ?), (?, ?), (?, ?)

;; Explicit columns
(sql/format
  {:insert-into [:users [:name :email]]
   :values [["Alice" "alice@example.com"]
            ["Bob" "bob@example.com"]]})
;; INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES (?, ?), (?, ?)

;; RETURNING (PostgreSQL)
(sql/format
  {:insert-into :users
   :values [{:name "Alice"}]
   :returning [:id :created_at]})
;; INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?) RETURNING id, created_at

;; INSERT ... SELECT
(sql/format
  {:insert-into [:archived_users [:id :name :email]]
   :select [:id :name :email]
   :from [:users]
   :where [:< :last_login #inst "2023-01-01"]})
;; INSERT INTO archived_users (id, name, email) SELECT id, name, email FROM users WHERE last_login < ?
```

**Using Helpers**
```clojure
(require '[honey.sql.helpers :as h])

(-> (h/insert-into :users)
    (h/values [{:name "Alice" :email "alice@example.com"}])
    (h/returning :id)
    sql/format)

;; Columns helper
(-> (h/insert-into :users)
    (h/columns :name :email :role)
    (h/values [["Alice" "alice@example.com" "user"]
               ["Bob" "bob@example.com" "admin"]])
    sql/format)
```

**UPDATE**
```clojure
;; Basic update
(sql/format
  {:update :users
   :set {:name "Alicia" :updated_at [:now]}
   :where [:= :id 1]})
;; => ["UPDATE users SET name = ?, updated_at = NOW() WHERE id = ?" "Alicia" 1]

;; Increment/decrement
(sql/format
  {:update :products
   :set {:stock [:- :stock 1]
         :times_sold [:+ :times_sold 1]}
   :where [:= :id 123]})
;; UPDATE products SET stock = stock - ?, times_sold = times_sold + ? WHERE id = ?

;; With FROM (PostgreSQL)
(sql/format
  {:update :orders
   :set {:status "shipped"}
   :from [:shipments]
   :where [:and
           [:= :shipments.order_id :orders.id]
           [:= :shipments.status "delivered"]]})

;; RETURNING
(sql/format
  {:update :users
   :set {:password_hash "new_hash"}
   :where [:= :id 1]
   :returning [:id :email :updated_at]})

;; Conditional update with CASE
(sql/format
  {:update :products
   :set {:price [:case
                  [:< :stock 10] [:* :price 1.1]  ; Low stock: +10%
                  [:> :stock 100] [:* :price 0.9]  ; High stock: -10%
                  :else :price]}
   :where [:= :category "electronics"]})
```

**DELETE**
```clojure
;; Basic delete
(sql/format
  {:delete-from :users
   :where [:= :id 1]})
;; => ["DELETE FROM users WHERE id = ?" 1]

;; Delete with subquery
(sql/format
  {:delete-from :sessions
   :where [:in :user_id
           {:select [:id]
            :from [:users]
            :where [:= :banned true]}]})

;; Delete all (careful!)
(sql/format
  {:delete-from :temp_logs})
;; DELETE FROM temp_logs

;; RETURNING
(sql/format
  {:delete-from :notifications
   :where [:< :created_at #inst "2024-01-01"]
   :returning [:id :user_id]})

;; Truncate (faster for all rows)
(sql/format
  {:truncate :logs})
;; TRUNCATE logs
```

**UPSERT (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT)**
```clojure
;; PostgreSQL ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE
(sql/format
  {:insert-into :users
   :values [{:email "alice@example.com" :name "Alice" :login_count 1}]
   :on-conflict [:email]
   :do-update-set [:name :login_count]})
;; INSERT INTO users (email, name, login_count) VALUES (?, ?, ?)
;; ON CONFLICT (email) DO UPDATE SET name = EXCLUDED.name, login_count = EXCLUDED.login_count

;; Increment on conflict
(sql/format
  {:insert-into :page_views
   :values [{:page_id 123 :view_count 1}]
   :on-conflict [:page_id]
   :do-update-set {:view_count [:+ :page_views.view_count 1]}})
;; ON CONFLICT (page_id) DO UPDATE SET view_count = page_views.view_count + 1

;; ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
(sql/format
  {:insert-into :users
   :values [{:email "alice@example.com" :name "Alice"}]
   :on-conflict [:email]
   :do-nothing true})
;; INSERT INTO users (email, name) VALUES (?, ?) ON CONFLICT (email) DO NOTHING

;; MySQL INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE
(sql/format
  {:insert-into :users
   :values [{:email "alice@example.com" :name "Alice"}]
   :on-duplicate-key-update {:name :values.name}}
  {:dialect :mysql})
```

**Batch Operations**
```clojure
(defn batch-insert! [ds table records]
  (when (seq records)
    (jdbc/execute! ds
      (sql/format
        {:insert-into table
         :values records}))))

(defn batch-upsert! [ds table records conflict-keys update-keys]
  (when (seq records)
    (jdbc/execute! ds
      (sql/format
        {:insert-into table
         :values records
         :on-conflict conflict-keys
         :do-update-set update-keys}))))

;; Usage
(batch-upsert! ds :products
  [{:sku "ABC" :name "Product A" :price 10}
   {:sku "DEF" :name "Product B" :price 20}]
  [:sku]
  [:name :price])
```

**Transaction Example**
```clojure
(defn transfer-funds! [ds from-id to-id amount]
  (jdbc/with-transaction [tx ds]
    ;; Deduct from source
    (jdbc/execute! tx
      (sql/format
        {:update :accounts
         :set {:balance [:- :balance amount]}
         :where [:and
                 [:= :id from-id]
                 [:>= :balance amount]]}))
    
    ;; Add to destination
    (jdbc/execute! tx
      (sql/format
        {:update :accounts
         :set {:balance [:+ :balance amount]}
         :where [:= :id to-id]}))
    
    ;; Log transaction
    (jdbc/execute! tx
      (sql/format
        {:insert-into :transactions
         :values [{:from_account from-id
                   :to_account to-id
                   :amount amount
                   :created_at [:now]}]}))))
```
What is Integrant and how do I set up a basic system?

Integrant is a dependency injection and lifecycle management library for Clojure. It helps you build systems from independent components with managed startup/shutdown.

**Setup**
```clojure
;; deps.edn
{:deps {integrant/integrant {:mvn/version "0.8.1"}}}

(require '[integrant.core :as ig])
```

**Core Concepts**
- **Configuration**: EDN map describing your system
- **Keys**: Keywords identifying components (usually namespaced)
- **init-key**: Multimethod to initialize a component
- **halt-key!**: Multimethod to shut down a component
- **refs**: Dependencies between components using `#ig/ref`

**Basic System**
```clojure
;; 1. Define configuration
(def config
  {:db/connection {:host "localhost"
                   :port 5432
                   :database "myapp"}
   :app/server {:port 3000
                :db #ig/ref :db/connection}})

;; 2. Implement init-key for each component
(defmethod ig/init-key :db/connection [_ {:keys [host port database]}]
  (println "Connecting to database" database)
  {:connection (create-db-connection host port database)})

(defmethod ig/init-key :app/server [_ {:keys [port db]}]
  (println "Starting server on port" port)
  (start-http-server {:port port :db db}))

;; 3. Implement halt-key! for cleanup
(defmethod ig/halt-key! :db/connection [_ conn]
  (println "Closing database connection")
  (close-connection (:connection conn)))

(defmethod ig/halt-key! :app/server [_ server]
  (println "Stopping server")
  (stop-http-server server))

;; 4. Start the system
(def system (ig/init config))
;; Prints:
;; Connecting to database myapp
;; Starting server on port 3000

;; 5. Stop the system
(ig/halt! system)
;; Prints:
;; Stopping server
;; Closing database connection
```

**Dependency Resolution**
```clojure
;; Integrant initializes components in dependency order
;; #ig/ref creates a dependency

(def config
  {;; No dependencies - initialized first
   :config/env {:profile :production}
   
   ;; Depends on :config/env
   :db/pool {:env #ig/ref :config/env
             :min-connections 5}
   
   ;; Depends on :db/pool
   :app/handler {:db #ig/ref :db/pool}
   
   ;; Depends on :app/handler
   :app/server {:port 3000
                :handler #ig/ref :app/handler}})

;; Init order: :config/env -> :db/pool -> :app/handler -> :app/server
;; Halt order: :app/server -> :app/handler -> :db/pool -> :config/env (reverse)
```

**Loading Config from EDN**
```clojure
;; resources/config.edn
{:db/connection {:host "localhost"
                 :port 5432
                 :database "myapp"}
 :app/server {:port 3000
              :db #ig/ref :db/connection}}

;; Load with reader
(require '[clojure.edn :as edn]
         '[clojure.java.io :as io])

(defn load-config [path]
  (-> path
      io/resource
      slurp
      (ig/read-string)))  ; Use ig/read-string for #ig/ref support

(def config (load-config "config.edn"))
(def system (ig/init config))
```

**Development Workflow**
```clojure
;; In dev, store system in atom for REPL reloading
(defonce system (atom nil))

(defn start []
  (reset! system (ig/init config)))

(defn stop []
  (when @system
    (ig/halt! @system)
    (reset! system nil)))

(defn restart []
  (stop)
  (start))

;; Or use integrant.repl for better workflow
```
How do I use integrant.repl for REPL-driven development?

integrant.repl provides convenient REPL workflow with automatic system management.

**Setup**
```clojure
;; deps.edn
{:deps {integrant/integrant {:mvn/version "0.8.1"}}
 :aliases {:dev {:extra-deps {integrant/repl {:mvn/version "0.3.3"}}}}}
```

**Basic REPL Setup**
```clojure
;; dev/user.clj
(ns user
  (:require [integrant.core :as ig]
            [integrant.repl :as ig-repl :refer [clear go halt prep init reset reset-all]]
            [integrant.repl.state :refer [config system]]))

;; Define your config or load from file
(defn get-config []
  {:db/connection {:host "localhost" :port 5432}
   :app/server {:port 3000 :db #ig/ref :db/connection}})

;; Set the config loader
(ig-repl/set-prep! get-config)
```

**REPL Commands**
```clojure
;; In REPL:
(require '[user :refer :all])  ; or (in-ns 'user)

;; Start system
(go)      ; Calls prep then init
;; => :initiated

;; Access running system
system    ; The running system map
config    ; The current config

(:db/connection system)  ; Get specific component

;; Stop system  
(halt)
;; => :halted

;; Restart (halt + go)
(reset)
;; => :resumed

;; Clear state and restart (useful after code changes)
(reset-all)  ; Clears, reloads namespaces, restarts
```

**Loading Config from File**
```clojure
(ns user
  (:require [integrant.core :as ig]
            [integrant.repl :as ig-repl :refer [go halt reset]]
            [clojure.java.io :as io]))

(defn read-config []
  (-> "config.edn"
      io/resource
      slurp
      ig/read-string))

(ig-repl/set-prep! read-config)

;; Now changes to config.edn are picked up on reset
```

**Environment-Specific Config**
```clojure
;; resources/config.edn (base)
{:db/connection {:host "localhost" :port 5432}}

;; resources/dev/config.edn (dev overrides)
{:db/connection {:database "myapp_dev"}}

;; resources/test/config.edn (test overrides)
{:db/connection {:database "myapp_test"}}

;; dev/user.clj
(defn read-config []
  (let [base (-> "config.edn" io/resource slurp ig/read-string)
        env (-> "dev/config.edn" io/resource slurp ig/read-string)]
    (deep-merge base env)))  ; You'd implement deep-merge

(ig-repl/set-prep! read-config)
```

**Suspend and Resume (for faster reloading)**
```clojure
;; Define suspend-key! for components that support it
(defmethod ig/suspend-key! :app/server [_ server]
  ;; Keep server running but mark as suspended
  (println "Suspending server"))

(defmethod ig/resume-key :app/server [key opts old-opts old-impl]
  (if (= opts old-opts)
    (do (println "Resuming server with same config")
        old-impl)  ; Reuse existing server
    (do (ig/halt-key! key old-impl)
        (ig/init-key key opts))))  ; Restart with new config

;; In REPL
(reset)  ; Uses suspend/resume if available - faster!
```

**Complete Dev Setup**
```clojure
;; dev/user.clj
(ns user
  (:require [integrant.core :as ig]
            [integrant.repl :as ig-repl :refer [clear go halt prep init reset reset-all]]
            [integrant.repl.state :refer [config system]]
            [clojure.tools.namespace.repl :as repl]
            [clojure.java.io :as io]))

;; Prevent reloading dev namespace
(repl/disable-reload! (find-ns 'user))

;; Config loading
(defn read-config []
  (-> "config.edn" io/resource slurp ig/read-string))

(ig-repl/set-prep! read-config)

;; Convenience functions
(defn db [] (:db/connection system))
(defn server [] (:app/server system))

;; Refresh code
(defn refresh []
  (repl/refresh))

(defn refresh-all []
  (repl/refresh-all))

(comment
  ;; REPL workflow
  (go)           ; Start
  (halt)         ; Stop
  (reset)        ; Restart
  (reset-all)    ; Full refresh and restart
  
  ;; Access components
  (db)           ; Get database
  (server)       ; Get server
  
  ;; When you change code
  (reset)        ; Restart with code changes
  )
```

**Tips for REPL Development**
```clojure
;; 1. Keep system startup fast
;; Don't do heavy work in init-key if possible

;; 2. Use suspend/resume for stateful components
;; Avoids full restart for config changes

;; 3. Make config a function, not a value
;; So it's re-read on each reset
(ig-repl/set-prep! read-config)  ; Good - re-reads each time
(ig-repl/set-prep! (constantly my-config))  ; Bad - static

;; 4. Use comment blocks for REPL experiments
(comment
  (go)
  (reset)
  ;; Experiment with your running system
  (:app/handler system)
  )
```
How do I create components with dependencies in Integrant?

Integrant uses `#ig/ref` to declare dependencies between components. The system initializes in dependency order.

**Ref Syntax**
```clojure
;; Reference another component
#ig/ref :component/key

;; In config
{:db/pool {:url "jdbc:postgresql://localhost/mydb"}
 :api/handler {:db #ig/ref :db/pool}}
```

**Full Example: Web Application**
```clojure
(ns myapp.system
  (:require [integrant.core :as ig]))

;; Config with dependency graph
(def config
  {;; Config loading - no dependencies
   :config/env {:profile :development
                :secret-key "dev-key"}
   
   ;; Database pool - depends on config
   :db/pool {:env #ig/ref :config/env
             :jdbc-url "jdbc:postgresql://localhost/mydb"
             :max-connections 10}
   
   ;; Cache - no dependencies
   :cache/redis {:host "localhost"
                 :port 6379}
   
   ;; Service layer - depends on db and cache
   :service/users {:db #ig/ref :db/pool
                   :cache #ig/ref :cache/redis}
   
   ;; HTTP handler - depends on services
   :api/handler {:users-service #ig/ref :service/users
                 :env #ig/ref :config/env}
   
   ;; Web server - depends on handler
   :web/server {:port 3000
                :handler #ig/ref :api/handler}})

;; Implementation
(defmethod ig/init-key :config/env [_ opts]
  (println "Loading config for" (:profile opts))
  opts)

(defmethod ig/init-key :db/pool [_ {:keys [jdbc-url max-connections]}]
  (println "Creating connection pool")
  ;; Return HikariCP pool or similar
  {:pool (create-pool jdbc-url max-connections)})

(defmethod ig/halt-key! :db/pool [_ {:keys [pool]}]
  (println "Closing connection pool")
  (.close pool))

(defmethod ig/init-key :cache/redis [_ {:keys [host port]}]
  (println "Connecting to Redis")
  (connect-redis host port))

(defmethod ig/halt-key! :cache/redis [_ conn]
  (println "Closing Redis connection")
  (close-redis conn))

(defmethod ig/init-key :service/users [_ {:keys [db cache]}]
  (println "Creating users service")
  ;; db and cache are already initialized values
  {:db db :cache cache})  ; Or create service record/protocol

(defmethod ig/init-key :api/handler [_ {:keys [users-service env]}]
  (println "Creating API handler")
  (create-ring-handler users-service env))

(defmethod ig/init-key :web/server [_ {:keys [port handler]}]
  (println "Starting server on port" port)
  (start-jetty handler {:port port :join? false}))

(defmethod ig/halt-key! :web/server [_ server]
  (println "Stopping server")
  (.stop server))
```

**Multiple Refs**
```clojure
;; Component can depend on multiple others
{:service/reporting {:db #ig/ref :db/pool
                     :cache #ig/ref :cache/redis
                     :email #ig/ref :email/client
                     :config #ig/ref :config/env}}

(defmethod ig/init-key :service/reporting [_ deps]
  ;; deps = {:db <pool> :cache <redis> :email <client> :config <env>}
  (map->ReportingService deps))
```

**Composite Keys (Multiple Instances)**
```clojure
;; Use vectors for composite keys to have multiple instances
{:adapter/http {:port 3000}
 :adapter/grpc {:port 9000}
 
 [:handler/api :v1] {:prefix "/v1" :db #ig/ref :db/pool}
 [:handler/api :v2] {:prefix "/v2" :db #ig/ref :db/pool}}

;; Implement with derive for shared behavior
(derive :adapter/http :adapter/any)
(derive :adapter/grpc :adapter/any)

(defmethod ig/init-key :adapter/any [key opts]
  (println "Starting adapter" key "on port" (:port opts)))

;; Or implement each
(defmethod ig/init-key [:handler/api :v1] [_ opts]
  (create-v1-handler opts))

(defmethod ig/init-key [:handler/api :v2] [_ opts]
  (create-v2-handler opts))
```

**Refset (Set of Refs)**
```clojure
;; Reference multiple components as a set
{[:handler :users] {:db #ig/ref :db/pool}
 [:handler :products] {:db #ig/ref :db/pool}
 [:handler :orders] {:db #ig/ref :db/pool}
 
 :router {:handlers #ig/refset :handler}}  ; All :handler/* components

(defmethod ig/init-key :router [_ {:keys [handlers]}]
  ;; handlers is a set of initialized handler components
  (create-router (into [] handlers)))
```

**Ref with Selection**
```clojure
;; Sometimes you need partial ref
(require '[integrant.core :as ig])

;; Ref only specific keys from component
{:db/pool {:primary {:url "jdbc:postgresql://primary/db"}
           :replica {:url "jdbc:postgresql://replica/db"}}
 
 :service/write {:db #ig/ref [:db/pool :primary]}
 :service/read {:db #ig/ref [:db/pool :replica]}}
```

**Dependency Graph Visualization**
```clojure
;; You can see the dependency order
(ig/dependency-graph config)

;; Returns a graph showing:
;; :config/env -> ()
;; :db/pool -> (:config/env)
;; :cache/redis -> ()
;; :service/users -> (:db/pool :cache/redis)
;; :api/handler -> (:service/users :config/env)
;; :web/server -> (:api/handler)
```

```clojure
;; src/myapp/main.clj
(ns myapp.main
  (:require [aero.core :as aero]
            [clojure.java.io :as io]
            [integrant.core :as ig])
  (:gen-class))

;; Register Integrant readers with Aero
(defmethod aero/reader 'ig/ref [_ _ value]
  (ig/ref value))

(defn read-config [profile]
  (-> "config.edn"
      io/resource
      (aero/read-config {:profile profile})))

(defn -main [& args]

        config (read-config profile)]
    (println "Starting with profile:" profile)
    
    ;; Load implementation namespaces
    (ig/load-namespaces config)
    
    ;; Start system
    (let [system (ig/init config)]
      ;; Add shutdown hook
      (.addShutdownHook
        (Runtime/getRuntime)
        (Thread. #(do (println "Shutting down...")
                      (ig/halt! system))))
      
      (println "System started"))))
```

How do I test components and systems with Integrant?

Testing Integrant systems requires strategies for isolation, mocking, and partial system startup.

**Test Fixtures**
```clojure
(ns myapp.test-fixtures
  (:require [integrant.core :as ig]
            [clojure.java.io :as io]))

(defn load-test-config []
  (-> "test-config.edn"
      io/resource
      slurp
      ig/read-string))

;; Fixture for full system
(def ^:dynamic *system* nil)

(defn with-system [f]
  (let [config (load-test-config)
        system (ig/init config)]
    (try
      (binding [*system* system]
        (f))
      (finally
        (ig/halt! system)))))

;; Use in tests
(ns myapp.handler-test
  (:require [clojure.test :refer :all]
            [myapp.test-fixtures :refer [*system* with-system]]))

(use-fixtures :once with-system)

(deftest test-handler
  (let [handler (:api/handler *system*)]
    (is (= 200 (:status (handler {:request-method :get :uri "/health"}))))))
```

**Partial System Startup**
```clojure
;; Only start specific keys
(def full-config
  {:db/pool {...}
   :cache/redis {...}
   :service/users {:db #ig/ref :db/pool :cache #ig/ref :cache/redis}
   :api/handler {:users #ig/ref :service/users}
   :web/server {:handler #ig/ref :api/handler}})

;; Start only what you need
(def test-system 
  (ig/init full-config [:db/pool :service/users]))
;; Only :db/pool and :service/users are initialized
;; :cache/redis NOT started (not in dependency chain of selected keys)

;; Test fixture for partial startup
(defn with-db-and-users [f]
  (let [system (ig/init (load-config) [:db/pool :service/users])]
    (try
      (binding [*system* system]
        (f))
      (finally
        (ig/halt! system)))))
```

**Mocking Components**
```clojure
;; Option 1: Override config
(def test-config
  (merge production-config
         {:db/pool {:type :mock}  ; Different config for tests
          :cache/redis {:type :mock}}))

(defmethod ig/init-key :db/pool [_ {:keys [type] :as opts}]
  (if (= type :mock)
    (create-mock-db)  ; Return mock
    (create-real-db opts)))  ; Real implementation

;; Option 2: Different keys for test implementations
(derive ::mock-db :db/pool)

(defmethod ig/init-key ::mock-db [_ _]
  (atom {}))  ; Simple in-memory mock

(def test-config
  {::mock-db {}
   :service/users {:db #ig/ref ::mock-db}})

;; Option 3: Protocol-based mocking
(defprotocol Database
  (find-user [this id])
  (save-user [this user]))

(defrecord PostgresDB [pool]
  Database
  (find-user [_ id] (query-user pool id))
  (save-user [_ user] (insert-user pool user)))

(defrecord MockDB [data]
  Database
  (find-user [_ id] (get @data id))
  (save-user [_ user] (swap! data assoc (:id user) user)))

(defmethod ig/init-key :db/postgres [_ opts]
  (->PostgresDB (create-pool opts)))

(defmethod ig/init-key :db/mock [_ _]
  (->MockDB (atom {})))
```

**Test Config Merging**
```clojure
(ns myapp.test-config
  (:require [integrant.core :as ig]
            [clojure.java.io :as io]))

(defn deep-merge [& maps]
  (apply merge-with
    (fn [v1 v2]
      (if (and (map? v1) (map? v2))
        (deep-merge v1 v2)
        v2))
    maps))

(defn test-config [overrides]
  (deep-merge
    (-> "config.edn" io/resource slurp ig/read-string)
    {:db/pool {:database "myapp_test"}
     :web/server {:port 0}}  ; Random available port
    overrides))

;; Usage

  (let [system (ig/init (test-config {:cache/redis {:ttl 1}}))]
    (try
      ;; Test with 1 second cache TTL
      (finally
        (ig/halt! system)))))
```

```clojure
            [ring.mock.request :as mock]))

(def ^:dynamic *system* nil)

   :service/users {:db #ig/ref :db/pool}
   :api/handler {:users #ig/ref :service/users}})
```

What is Ring and how do I create a basic HTTP server?

Ring is Clojure's HTTP server abstraction. It's a specification for handlers, middleware, and request/response maps - similar to Python's WSGI or Ruby's Rack. **Core Concepts** - **Handler**: Function that takes a request map, returns a response map - **Middleware**: Function that wraps handlers to add functionality - **Request/Response**: Clojure maps with specific keys **Setup** ```clojure ;; deps.edn {:deps {ring/ring-core {:mvn/version "1.10.0"} ring/ring-jetty-adapter {:mvn/version "1.10.0"}}} ``` **Hello World** ```clojure (require '[ring.adapter.jetty :as jetty]) ;; Handler - a function that returns a response map (defn handler [request] {:status 200 :headers {"Content-Type" "text/plain"} :body "Hello, World!"}) ;; Start server (jetty/run-jetty handler {:port 3000}) ;; Server runs on http://localhost:3000 ``` **Request Map** ```clojure ;; Ring request map structure {:server-port 3000 :server-name "localhost" :remote-addr "127.0.0.1" :uri "/users/123" :query-string "active=true" :scheme :http :request-method :get :protocol "HTTP/1.1" :headers {"host" "localhost:3000" "accept" "application/json" "user-agent" "curl/7.64.1"} :body #object[InputStream]} ;; Access request parts (defn handler [request] (let [method (:request-method request) ; :get, :post, :put, :delete uri (:uri request) ; "/users/123" params (:query-string request) ; "active=true" headers (:headers request)] ; {"host" "localhost"...} {:status 200 :body (str "Method: " method " URI: " uri)})) ``` **Response Map** ```clojure ;; Basic response {:status 200 :headers {"Content-Type" "text/html"} :body "

Hello

"} ;; JSON response {:status 200 :headers {"Content-Type" "application/json"} :body "{\"message\": \"success\"}"} ;; Redirect {:status 302 :headers {"Location" "/dashboard"} :body ""} ;; Not Found {:status 404 :headers {"Content-Type" "text/plain"} :body "Not Found"} ;; Error {:status 500 :headers {"Content-Type" "text/plain"} :body "Internal Server Error"} ``` **Response Helpers** ```clojure (require '[ring.util.response :as response]) ;; Create responses easily (response/response "Hello") ; 200 with body (response/not-found "Page not found") ; 404 (response/bad-request "Invalid input"); 400 (response/redirect "/login") ; 302 redirect (response/created "/users/123") ; 201 with Location header ;; Add headers (-> (response/response "Hello") (response/content-type "text/plain") (response/header "X-Custom" "value")) ;; Status helpers (response/status (response/response "OK") 201) ``` **Routing (Manual)** ```clojure (defn handler [request] (let [{:keys [uri request-method]} request] (case [request-method uri] [:get "/"] {:status 200 :body "Home"} [:get "/about"] {:status 200 :body "About"} [:get "/users"] {:status 200 :body "List users"} [:post "/users"] {:status 201 :body "User created"} ;; Default - 404 {:status 404 :body "Not Found"}))) ``` **Using Compojure for Routing** ```clojure ;; deps.edn {:deps {compojure/compojure {:mvn/version "1.7.0"}}} (require '[compojure.core :refer [defroutes GET POST PUT DELETE]] '[compojure.route :as route]) (defroutes app (GET "/" [] "Home") (GET "/about" [] "About") (GET "/users" [] "List users") (GET "/users/:id" [id] (str "User " id)) (POST "/users" [] "Create user") (PUT "/users/:id" [id] (str "Update user " id)) (DELETE "/users/:id" [id] (str "Delete user " id)) (route/not-found "Not Found")) (jetty/run-jetty app {:port 3000}) ``` **Server Options** ```clojure ;; Development - auto-reload friendly (def server (jetty/run-jetty #'handler ; Use var for REPL reloading {:port 3000 :join? false})) ; Don't block thread ;; Stop server (.stop server) ;; Production (jetty/run-jetty handler {:port 3000 :host "0.0.0.0" ; Listen on all interfaces :join? true ; Block main thread :ssl? true :ssl-port 443 :keystore "keystore.jks" :key-password "secret"}) ```
How do I create and use Ring middleware?

Middleware in Ring are functions that wrap handlers to add cross-cutting functionality like logging, authentication, or parsing.

**Middleware Pattern**
```clojure
;; Middleware is a function that takes a handler and returns a new handler
(defn wrap-example [handler]
  (fn [request]
    ;; Before: modify request or do pre-processing
    (let [response (handler request)]  ; Call wrapped handler
      ;; After: modify response or do post-processing
      response)))

;; Apply middleware
(def app (wrap-example handler))
```

**Logging Middleware**
```clojure
(defn wrap-logging [handler]
  (fn [request]
    (let [start (System/currentTimeMillis)
          {:keys [request-method uri]} request]
      (println "-->" (name request-method) uri)
      (let [response (handler request)
            elapsed (- (System/currentTimeMillis) start)]
        (println "<--" (:status response) (str elapsed "ms"))
        response))))

;; Usage
(def app (wrap-logging handler))
;; Logs:
;; --> GET /users
;; <-- 200 45ms
```

**Authentication Middleware**
```clojure
(defn wrap-authentication [handler]
  (fn [request]
    (let [token (get-in request [:headers "authorization"])]
      (if-let [user (when token (verify-token token))]
        ;; Add user to request
        (handler (assoc request :user user))
        ;; Return 401
        {:status 401
         :headers {"Content-Type" "application/json"}
         :body "{\"error\": \"Unauthorized\"}"}))))

;; Make some routes require auth
(defn wrap-require-auth [handler]
  (fn [request]
    (if (:user request)
      (handler request)
      {:status 401 :body "Authentication required"})))

;; Apply
(def public-handler 
  (-> handler
      wrap-authentication))  ; Adds :user if token valid

(def protected-handler
  (-> handler
      wrap-require-auth      ; Requires :user
      wrap-authentication))  ; Adds :user
```

**Error Handling Middleware**
```clojure
(defn wrap-exceptions [handler]
  (fn [request]
    (try
      (handler request)
      (catch Exception e
        (println "Error:" (.getMessage e))
        {:status 500
         :headers {"Content-Type" "application/json"}
         :body (str "{\"error\": \"" (.getMessage e) "\"}")}))
      (catch Throwable t
        (println "Critical error:" (.getMessage t))
        {:status 500
         :body "Internal Server Error"}))))

;; With custom exception types
(defn wrap-app-exceptions [handler]
  (fn [request]
    (try
      (handler request)
      (catch clojure.lang.ExceptionInfo e
        (let [{:keys [type status message]} (ex-data e)]
          (case type
            :validation {:status 400 :body message}
            :not-found {:status 404 :body message}
            :unauthorized {:status 401 :body message}
            {:status 500 :body "Server error"}))))))
```

**CORS Middleware**
```clojure
(defn wrap-cors [handler]
  (fn [request]
    (let [response (if (= :options (:request-method request))
                     {:status 200 :body ""}
                     (handler request))]
      (-> response
          (assoc-in [:headers "Access-Control-Allow-Origin"] "*")
          (assoc-in [:headers "Access-Control-Allow-Methods"] "GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS")
          (assoc-in [:headers "Access-Control-Allow-Headers"] "Content-Type, Authorization")))))
```

**Request Parsing Middleware**
```clojure
(require '[ring.middleware.params :refer [wrap-params]]
         '[ring.middleware.keyword-params :refer [wrap-keyword-params]]
         '[ring.middleware.json :refer [wrap-json-body wrap-json-response]])

;; Query params: "?name=alice&age=30"
;; wrap-params adds :query-params {"name" "alice" "age" "30"}
;; wrap-keyword-params converts to :params {:name "alice" :age "30"}

(def app
  (-> handler
      wrap-keyword-params
      wrap-params
      (wrap-json-body {:keywords? true})  ; Parse JSON body
      wrap-json-response))                 ; Serialize response as JSON
```

**Content Negotiation**
```clojure
(defn wrap-content-type [handler content-type]
  (fn [request]
    (let [response (handler request)]
      (if (get-in response [:headers "Content-Type"])
        response
        (assoc-in response [:headers "Content-Type"] content-type)))))

;; Default to JSON
(def app
  (-> handler
      (wrap-content-type "application/json")))
```

**Middleware with Configuration**
```clojure
(defn wrap-rate-limit [handler {:keys [max-requests window-ms]}]
  (let [requests (atom {})]  ; ip -> [timestamps]
    (fn [request]
      (let [ip (:remote-addr request)
            now (System/currentTimeMillis)
            cutoff (- now window-ms)
            recent (filter #(> % cutoff) (get @requests ip []))]
        (if (>= (count recent) max-requests)
          {:status 429 :body "Too Many Requests"}
          (do
            (swap! requests assoc ip (conj recent now))
            (handler request)))))))

;; Usage
(def app
  (-> handler
      (wrap-rate-limit {:max-requests 100 :window-ms 60000})))
```

**Composing Middleware**
```clojure
;; Using ->
(def app
  (-> handler
      wrap-logging
      wrap-exceptions
      wrap-authentication
      wrap-keyword-params
      wrap-params
      wrap-json-body
      wrap-json-response
      wrap-cors))

;; Middleware applied inside-out:
;; Request  -> cors -> json-body -> params -> auth -> exceptions -> logging -> handler
;; Response <- cors <- json-resp <- params <- auth <- exceptions <- logging <- handler

;; Using comp (reverse order)
(def middleware
  (comp wrap-cors
        wrap-json-response
        wrap-json-body
        wrap-params
        wrap-keyword-params
        wrap-authentication
        wrap-exceptions
        wrap-logging))

(def app (middleware handler))
```

**Conditional Middleware**
```clojure
(defn wrap-if [handler pred middleware]
  (if pred
    (middleware handler)
    handler))

;; Only apply in production
(def app
  (-> handler
      (wrap-if (= :prod env) wrap-ssl-redirect)
      (wrap-if (= :dev env) wrap-reload)))

;; Route-specific middleware
(defn wrap-for-routes [handler routes middleware]
  (fn [request]
    (if (some #(re-matches % (:uri request)) routes)
      ((middleware handler) request)
      (handler request))))

(def app
  (-> handler
      (wrap-for-routes [#"/api/.*" #"/admin/.*"] wrap-authentication)))
```
How do I handle different content types and JSON in Ring?

Ring handles different content types through middleware for parsing requests and formatting responses.

**JSON Handling**
```clojure
;; deps.edn
{:deps {ring/ring-json {:mvn/version "0.5.1"}
        ;; or use cheshire directly
        cheshire/cheshire {:mvn/version "5.12.0"}}}

(require '[ring.middleware.json :refer [wrap-json-body wrap-json-response]]
         '[cheshire.core :as json])
```

**Parsing JSON Requests**
```clojure
;; wrap-json-body parses JSON body into :body
(def app
  (-> handler
      (wrap-json-body {:keywords? true   ; Convert keys to keywords
                       :bigdecimals? false})))

;; Handler receives parsed JSON
(defn create-user [request]
  (let [{:keys [name email]} (:body request)]  ; Already parsed!
    (println "Creating user:" name email)
    {:status 201
     :body {:id 1 :name name :email email}}))

;; Manual JSON parsing
(defn handler [request]
  (let [body (-> request :body slurp (json/parse-string true))]
    {:status 200
     :body body}))
```

**JSON Responses**
```clojure
;; wrap-json-response converts Clojure data to JSON
(def app
  (-> handler
      wrap-json-response  ; Automatically converts maps/vectors to JSON
      (wrap-json-body {:keywords? true})))

(defn list-users [_]
  {:status 200
   :body [{:id 1 :name "Alice"}
          {:id 2 :name "Bob"}]})
;; Response body is automatically JSON: [{"id":1,"name":"Alice"},...]

;; Manual JSON response
(require '[cheshire.core :as json])

(defn list-users [_]
  {:status 200
   :headers {"Content-Type" "application/json"}
   :body (json/generate-string [{:id 1 :name "Alice"}])})
```

**Form Data**
```clojure
(require '[ring.middleware.params :refer [wrap-params]]
         '[ring.middleware.keyword-params :refer [wrap-keyword-params]])

;; For application/x-www-form-urlencoded
(def app
  (-> handler
      wrap-keyword-params  ; String keys -> keyword keys
      wrap-params))        ; Parse query string & form body

;; Handler
(defn login [request]
  (let [{:keys [username password]} (:params request)]
    (if (valid-credentials? username password)
      {:status 200 :body "Login successful"}
      {:status 401 :body "Invalid credentials"})))

;; POST /login with body: username=alice&password=secret
;; :params = {:username "alice" :password "secret"}
```

**Multipart File Upload**
```clojure
(require '[ring.middleware.multipart-params :refer [wrap-multipart-params]])

(def app
  (-> handler
      wrap-keyword-params
      wrap-multipart-params))  ; Parse multipart/form-data

;; File upload handler
(defn upload-file [request]
  (let [{:keys [file]} (:params request)]
    ;; file is a map with :filename, :content-type, :tempfile, :size
    (println "Received:" (:filename file) (:size file) "bytes")
    
    ;; Copy temp file to permanent location
    (io/copy (:tempfile file) 
             (io/file "uploads" (:filename file)))
    
    {:status 200
     :body {:message "File uploaded"
            :filename (:filename file)}}))

;; curl -F "file=@photo.jpg" http://localhost:3000/upload
```

**Content Negotiation**
```clojure
;; Check Accept header for response format
(defn handler [request]
  (let [accept (get-in request [:headers "accept"] "application/json")
        data {:users [{:id 1 :name "Alice"}]}]
    (cond
      (clojure.string/includes? accept "application/json")
      {:status 200
       :headers {"Content-Type" "application/json"}
       :body (json/generate-string data)}
      
      (clojure.string/includes? accept "application/edn")
      {:status 200
       :headers {"Content-Type" "application/edn"}
       :body (pr-str data)}
      
      (clojure.string/includes? accept "text/html")
      {:status 200
       :headers {"Content-Type" "text/html"}
       :body (render-html data)}
      
      :else
      {:status 406 :body "Not Acceptable"})))
```

**Using Muuntaja (Recommended)**
```clojure
;; deps.edn - better content negotiation library
{:deps {metosin/muuntaja {:mvn/version "0.6.8"}}}

(require '[muuntaja.core :as m]
         '[muuntaja.middleware :as muuntaja])

;; Muuntaja handles JSON, EDN, Transit automatically
(def app
  (-> handler
      (muuntaja/wrap-format m/instance)))

;; Automatically:
;; - Parses request body based on Content-Type
;; - Formats response based on Accept header
;; - Handles JSON, EDN, Transit out of the box

(defn handler [request]
  ;; :body-params contains parsed body
  (let [{:keys [name email]} (:body-params request)]
    {:status 200
     :body {:message "Created"
            :user {:name name :email email}}}))

;; Request with Content-Type: application/json -> parses JSON
;; Request with Accept: application/edn -> returns EDN
```

**Streaming Responses**
```clojure
;; Return InputStream for large files
(defn download-file [request]
  (let [file (io/file "large-file.zip")]
    {:status 200
     :headers {"Content-Type" "application/zip"
               "Content-Length" (str (.length file))
               "Content-Disposition" "attachment; filename=\"large-file.zip\""}
     :body (io/input-stream file)}))

;; Streaming with chunked transfer
(defn stream-events [request]
  (let [out (java.io.PipedOutputStream.)
        in (java.io.PipedInputStream. out)]
    ;; Start background thread to write events
    (future
      (with-open [writer (io/writer out)]
        (dotimes [i 10]
          (.write writer (str "data: Event " i "\n\n"))
          (.flush writer)
          (Thread/sleep 1000))))
    
    {:status 200
     :headers {"Content-Type" "text/event-stream"
               "Cache-Control" "no-cache"}
     :body in}))
```

```clojure
(ns myapp.handler
  (:require [ring.adapter.jetty :as jetty]
            [ring.middleware.session :refer [wrap-session]]
            [ring.middleware.params :refer [wrap-params]]
            [ring.middleware.keyword-params :refer [wrap-keyword-params]]
            [ring.middleware.json :refer [wrap-json-body wrap-json-response]]
            [ring.middleware.resource :refer [wrap-resource]]
            [ring.middleware.content-type :refer [wrap-content-type]]
            [ring.util.response :as response]))

(defn require-auth [handler]
  (fn [request]
    (if (get-in request [:session :user-id])
      (handler request)
      {:status 401 :body {:error "Unauthorized"}})))

(defn handler [{:keys [uri request-method session body]}]
  (case [request-method uri]
    [:post "/login"]
    (let [{:keys [username password]} body]
      (if (= [username password] ["admin" "secret"])
        {:status 200
         :session {:user-id 1 :username username}
         :body {:message "Logged in"}}
        {:status 401 :body {:error "Invalid credentials"}}))
    
    [:post "/logout"]
    {:status 200
     :session nil
     :body {:message "Logged out"}}
    
    [:get "/me"]
    (if-let [user-id (:user-id session)]
      {:status 200 :body {:user-id user-id :username (:username session)}}
      {:status 401 :body {:error "Not logged in"}})
    
    [:get "/protected"]
    ((require-auth
       (fn [req]
         {:status 200 :body {:data "Secret stuff"}}))
     {:uri uri :request-method request-method :session session})
    
    ;; Default
    {:status 404 :body {:error "Not found"}}))

(def app
  (-> handler
      wrap-json-response
      (wrap-json-body {:keywords? true})
      wrap-keyword-params
      wrap-params
      (wrap-session {:cookie-attrs {:http-only true :max-age 3600}})
      (wrap-resource "public")
      wrap-content-type))

(defn -main []
  (jetty/run-jetty app {:port 3000 :join? false}))
```

What is core.async and how do I use channels?

core.async is a Clojure library for asynchronous programming using channels and go blocks. It brings CSP (Communicating Sequential Processes) to Clojure.

**Setup**
```clojure
;; deps.edn
{:deps {org.clojure/core.async {:mvn/version "1.6.681"}}}

(require '[clojure.core.async :as async
           :refer [chan go go-loop <! >! <!! >!! close! put! take!
                   alts! alts!! timeout buffer sliding-buffer
                   dropping-buffer]])
```

**Core Concepts**
- **Channel**: Queue for passing values between threads/go blocks
- **go block**: Lightweight thread (parked, not OS thread)
- **<!** and **>!**: Take and put inside go blocks (parking)
- **<!!** and **>!!**: Take and put outside go blocks (blocking)

**Basic Channels**
```clojure
;; Create channel
(def ch (chan))         ; Unbuffered channel
(def ch (chan 10))      ; Buffered channel (holds 10 items)

;; Put and take (blocking - use outside go blocks)
(>!! ch "hello")        ; Put value (blocks if full)
(<!! ch)                ; Take value (blocks if empty)
;; => "hello"

;; Close channel
(close! ch)             ; No more puts allowed
(<!! ch)                ; Takes return nil when closed and empty
```

**Go Blocks**
```clojure
;; go blocks are lightweight "threads"
;; <! and >! park (don't block real thread)

(def ch (chan))

;; Producer
(go
  (dotimes [i 5]
    (>! ch i)           ; Put i to channel (parks if full)
    (println "Put" i))
  (close! ch))

;; Consumer
(go
  (loop []
    (when-let [v (<! ch)]  ; Take from channel (parks if empty)
      (println "Got" v)
      (recur))))

;; Output (interleaved):
;; Put 0
;; Got 0
;; Put 1
;; Got 1
;; ...
```

**go-loop (Common Pattern)**
```clojure
;; go-loop = (go (loop ...))
(def ch (chan))

;; Consumer with go-loop
(go-loop []
  (when-let [msg (<! ch)]
    (println "Processing:" msg)
    (recur)))

;; Producer
(go
  (doseq [x ["a" "b" "c"]]
    (>! ch x))
  (close! ch))
```

**Buffered Channels**
```clojure
;; Regular buffer - blocks when full
(def ch (chan 3))
(>!! ch 1)  ; ok
(>!! ch 2)  ; ok
(>!! ch 3)  ; ok
(>!! ch 4)  ; blocks! buffer full

;; Sliding buffer - drops oldest when full
(def ch (chan (sliding-buffer 3)))
(>!! ch 1) (>!! ch 2) (>!! ch 3)
(>!! ch 4)  ; Doesn't block, drops 1
(<!! ch)    ; => 2 (oldest remaining)

;; Dropping buffer - drops newest when full
(def ch (chan (dropping-buffer 3)))
(>!! ch 1) (>!! ch 2) (>!! ch 3)
(>!! ch 4)  ; Doesn't block, 4 is dropped
(<!! ch)    ; => 1 (4 was never added)
```

**Timeout Channels**
```clojure
;; timeout creates a channel that closes after ms
(let [ch (chan)
      t (timeout 1000)]  ; 1 second timeout
  (go
    (let [[v c] (alts! [ch t])]  ; Wait for either
      (if (= c t)
        (println "Timeout!")
        (println "Got:" v)))))

;; Timeout pattern
(defn fetch-with-timeout [ch timeout-ms]
  (go
    (let [[v c] (alts! [ch (timeout timeout-ms)])]
      (if v
        {:success v}
        {:error :timeout}))))
```

**alts! - Waiting on Multiple Channels**
```clojure
;; alts! waits on multiple channels, returns [value channel]
(let [ch1 (chan)
      ch2 (chan)]
  (go (>! ch1 "from ch1"))
  (go (>! ch2 "from ch2"))
  
  (go
    (let [[v ch] (alts! [ch1 ch2])]
      (condp = ch
        ch1 (println "Got from ch1:" v)
        ch2 (println "Got from ch2:" v)))))

;; With timeout
(go
  (let [[v ch] (alts! [data-chan (timeout 5000)])]
    (if v
      (process v)
      (println "Timed out waiting for data"))))

;; Priority (try channels in order)
(alts! [ch1 ch2 ch3] :priority true)
```

**put! and take! (Callback-based)**
```clojure
;; put! and take! are async with callbacks
;; Good for interop with callback-based code

(def ch (chan))

;; Async put
(put! ch "hello" (fn [success?]
                    (println "Put succeeded:" success?)))

;; Async take
(take! ch (fn [val]
            (println "Got:" val)))

;; No callback
(put! ch "hello")  ; Fire and forget
```
How do I use pipelines and transducers with core.async?

core.async integrates beautifully with transducers for efficient data processing.

**Channels with Transducers**
```clojure
(require '[clojure.core.async :as async :refer [chan go <! >! <!! >!! close!]])

;; Channel with transducer
(def ch (chan 10 (map inc)))  ; Buffer of 10, increment all values

(go (>! ch 1))
(<!! ch)  ; => 2 (1 + 1)

;; Composed transducers
(def ch (chan 10 (comp
                   (filter even?)
                   (map #(* % 2))
                   (take 5))))

;; Multiple transforms
(def process-xf
  (comp
    (map parse-json)
    (filter valid?)
    (map transform)
    (remove nil?)))

(def processing-chan (chan 100 process-xf))
```

**Exception Handler**
```clojure
;; Transducers can throw - provide exception handler
(def ch (chan 10 
          (map #(/ 100 %))  ; Division by zero possible
          (fn [ex]
            (println "Error:" (.getMessage ex))
            nil)))  ; Return value for error cases

(go (>! ch 0))  ; Would throw, but handler catches
```

**pipeline**
```clojure
;; pipeline runs transducer across multiple "threads" (go blocks)
(require '[clojure.core.async :refer [pipeline pipeline-blocking pipeline-async]])

(def in-ch (chan 100))
(def out-ch (chan 100))

;; 4 parallel workers
(pipeline 4                ; Parallelism
          out-ch           ; Output channel  
          (map expensive-transform)  ; Transducer
          in-ch)           ; Input channel

;; Producer
(go
  (doseq [item items]
    (>! in-ch item))
  (close! in-ch))

;; Consumer
(go-loop []
  (when-let [result (<! out-ch)]
    (process-result result)
    (recur)))
```

**pipeline-blocking vs pipeline-async**
```clojure
;; pipeline - for pure transforms (uses go blocks)
(pipeline 4 out (map transform) in)

;; pipeline-blocking - for blocking IO (uses real threads)
(pipeline-blocking 4 out 
  (map (fn [url] (http/get url)))  ; Blocking HTTP call
  in)

;; pipeline-async - for async operations
(pipeline-async 4 out
  (fn [val result-ch]
    ;; Put result to result-ch when done
    (async-fetch val #(do (async/>!! result-ch %) 
                          (async/close! result-ch))))
  in)
```

**onto-chan and to-chan**
```clojure
;; to-chan - collection to channel
(def ch (async/to-chan! [1 2 3 4 5]))
(<!! ch)  ; => 1
(<!! ch)  ; => 2

;; onto-chan! - put collection onto existing channel
(def ch (chan))
(async/onto-chan! ch [1 2 3] true)  ; true = close after

;; onto-chan! with false - don't close
(async/onto-chan! ch [1 2 3] false)
(async/onto-chan! ch [4 5 6] true)  ; Close after second batch
```

**into-chan**
```clojure
;; Collect channel into collection
(def ch (async/to-chan! [1 2 3 4 5]))

(<!! (async/into [] ch))  ; => [1 2 3 4 5]

;; With transformation
(def ch (chan 10 (map inc)))
(async/onto-chan! ch [1 2 3])
(<!! (async/into #{} ch))  ; => #{2 3 4}
```

**reduce over Channel**
```clojure
(def ch (async/to-chan! [1 2 3 4 5]))

;; Returns channel with final result
(def result-ch (async/reduce + 0 ch))
(<!! result-ch)  ; => 15

;; transduce
(def ch (async/to-chan! [1 2 3 4 5]))
(def result-ch (async/transduce (filter even?) + 0 ch))
(<!! result-ch)  ; => 6 (2 + 4)
```

**Pub/Sub**
```clojure
(require '[clojure.core.async :refer [pub sub unsub chan go-loop <! >!!]])

;; Create publisher from channel
(def events-ch (chan))
(def publisher (pub events-ch :type))  ; Dispatch on :type key

;; Create subscribers
(def user-events (chan))
(def order-events (chan))

(sub publisher :user user-events)   ; Subscribe to :user type
(sub publisher :order order-events) ; Subscribe to :order type

;; Consumers
(go-loop []
  (when-let [event (<! user-events)]
    (println "User event:" event)
    (recur)))

(go-loop []
  (when-let [event (<! order-events)]
    (println "Order event:" event)
    (recur)))

;; Publisher sends events
(>!! events-ch {:type :user :action :login :user-id 123})
;; => "User event: {:type :user ...}"

(>!! events-ch {:type :order :action :created :order-id 456})
;; => "Order event: {:type :order ...}"
```

**Mult (Broadcast)**
```clojure
(require '[clojure.core.async :refer [mult tap untap chan]])

;; mult broadcasts to multiple channels
(def source (chan))
(def m (mult source))

;; Tap into mult

(tap m consumer2)

(<!! consumer2)  ; => "hello"
```

How do I build a worker pool or rate limiter with core.async?

core.async is great for building concurrency patterns like worker pools and rate limiters.

**Worker Pool**
```clojure
(require '[clojure.core.async :as async
           :refer [chan go go-loop <! >! >!! <!! close! thread]])

(defn worker-pool
  "Creates n workers processing items from in-ch, results to out-ch"
  [n process-fn in-ch out-ch]
  (dotimes [i n]
    (go-loop []
      (when-let [item (<! in-ch)]
        (try
          (let [result (process-fn item)]
            (when result
              (>! out-ch result)))
          (catch Exception e
            (println "Worker" i "error:" (.getMessage e))))
        (recur))))
  out-ch)

;; Usage
(def jobs (chan 100))
(def results (chan 100))

;; Start 4 workers
(worker-pool 4 expensive-computation jobs results)

;; Submit jobs
(go
  (doseq [job job-list]
    (>! jobs job))
  (close! jobs))

;; Collect results
(go-loop [all-results []]
  (if-let [result (<! results)]
    (recur (conj all-results result))
    (println "All done:" (count all-results))))
```

**Worker Pool with Blocking Operations**
```clojure
;; For IO-bound work, use thread instead of go
(defn blocking-worker-pool [n process-fn in-ch out-ch]
  (dotimes [_ n]
    (thread
      (loop []
        (when-let [item (<!! in-ch)]
          (try
            (when-let [result (process-fn item)]  ; Can block!
              (>!! out-ch result))
            (catch Exception e
              (println "Error:" (.getMessage e))))
          (recur)))))
  out-ch)

;; Good for HTTP requests, database calls, file IO
(defn fetch-url [url]
  (:body (http/get url)))  ; Blocking call

(def urls-ch (chan 100))
(def results-ch (chan 100))

(blocking-worker-pool 10 fetch-url urls-ch results-ch)
```

**Rate Limiter**
```clojure
(defn rate-limiter
  "Limits throughput to n items per interval-ms"
  [n interval-ms in-ch out-ch]
  (let [tokens (chan n)]  ; Semaphore as channel
    ;; Fill with initial tokens
    (dotimes [_ n]
      (>!! tokens :token))
    
    ;; Token replenisher
    (go-loop []
      (<! (async/timeout interval-ms))
      (dotimes [_ n]
        (async/offer! tokens :token))  ; Non-blocking put
      (recur))
    
    ;; Rate-limited forwarder
    (go-loop []
      (when-let [item (<! in-ch)]
        (<! tokens)  ; Wait for token
        (>! out-ch item)
        (recur)))))

;; Usage: 10 items per second
(def unlimited (chan 1000))
(def limited (chan 1000))
(rate-limiter 10 1000 unlimited limited)
```

**Token Bucket Rate Limiter**
```clojure
(defn token-bucket
  "Token bucket rate limiter
   rate: tokens per second
   burst: max tokens (bucket size)"
  [rate burst]
  (let [tokens (atom burst)
        interval (/ 1000.0 rate)]
    ;; Refill tokens
    (go-loop []
      (<! (async/timeout (long interval)))
      (swap! tokens #(min burst (inc %)))
      (recur))
    
    ;; Return function that acquires token
    (fn acquire! []
      (loop []
        (if (pos? @tokens)
          (do (swap! tokens dec) true)
          (do (Thread/sleep 10) (recur)))))))

;; Usage
(def limiter (token-bucket 10 20))  ; 10/sec, burst of 20

(defn rate-limited-call [f & args]
  (limiter)  ; Wait for token
  (apply f args))
```

**Bounded Parallel Processing**
```clojure
(defn bounded-pmap
  "Like pmap but with bounded parallelism using core.async"
  [n f coll]
  (let [in-ch (chan)
        out-ch (chan)]
    ;; Start workers
    (dotimes [_ n]
      (go-loop []
        (when-let [[idx item] (<! in-ch)]
          (>! out-ch [idx (f item)])
          (recur))))
    
    ;; Submit work with index
    (let [indexed (map-indexed vector coll)
          cnt (count coll)]
      (go
        (doseq [item indexed]
          (>! in-ch item))
        (close! in-ch))
      
      ;; Collect and sort by original index
      (->> (repeatedly cnt #(<!! out-ch))
           (sort-by first)
           (map second)))))

;; Usage
(bounded-pmap 4 expensive-fn items)
```

**Request Coalescing (Debounce)**
```clojure
(defn debounce
  "Only forward last value received within wait-ms"
  [in-ch wait-ms]
  (let [out-ch (chan)]
    (go-loop [last-val nil
              timer nil]
      (let [ports (if timer [in-ch timer] [in-ch])
            [v ch] (async/alts! ports)]
        (condp = ch
          timer (do
                  (when last-val
                    (>! out-ch last-val))
                  (recur nil nil))
          in-ch (if v
                  (recur v (async/timeout wait-ms))
                  (close! out-ch)))))
    out-ch))

;; Usage - debounce search input
(def search-input (chan))
(def debounced (debounce search-input 300))

(go-loop []
  (when-let [query (<! debounced)]
    (perform-search query)
    (recur)))
```

**Batch Processing**
```clojure
(defn batch
  "Collect items into batches by size or timeout"
  [in-ch batch-size timeout-ms]
  (let [out-ch (chan)]
    (go-loop [batch []
              timer (async/timeout timeout-ms)]
      (let [[v ch] (async/alts! [in-ch timer])]
        (cond
          ;; Timeout - flush batch
          (= ch timer)
          (do
            (when (seq batch)
              (>! out-ch batch))
            (recur [] (async/timeout timeout-ms)))
          
          ;; Channel closed
          (nil? v)
          (do
            (when (seq batch)
              (>! out-ch batch))
            (close! out-ch))
          
          ;; Batch full
          (= (count batch) (dec batch-size))
          (do
            (>! out-ch (conj batch v))
            (recur [] (async/timeout timeout-ms)))
          
          ;; Add to batch
          :else
          (recur (conj batch v) timer))))
    out-ch))

;; Usage - batch database inserts
(def events (chan 1000))
(def batched (batch events 100 5000))  ; 100 items or 5 seconds

(go-loop []
  (when-let [batch (<! batched)]
    (db/insert-batch! batch)  ; Efficient batch insert
    (recur)))
```

**Circuit Breaker**
```clojure
(defn circuit-breaker
  [failure-threshold reset-timeout-ms]
  (let [failures (atom 0)
        state (atom :closed)  ; :closed, :open, :half-open
        last-failure (atom 0)]
    
    (fn [f]
      (case @state
        :open
        (if (> (- (System/currentTimeMillis) @last-failure) reset-timeout-ms)
          (do (reset! state :half-open)
              (try
                (let [result (f)]
                  (reset! state :closed)
                  (reset! failures 0)
                  result)
                (catch Exception e
                  (reset! state :open)
                  (reset! last-failure (System/currentTimeMillis))
                  (throw e))))
          (throw (ex-info "Circuit open" {:state :open})))
        
        (:closed :half-open)
        (try
          (let [result (f)]
            (when (= @state :half-open)
              (reset! state :closed)
              (reset! failures 0))
            result)
          (catch Exception e
            (swap! failures inc)
            (when (>= @failures failure-threshold)
              (reset! state :open)
              (reset! last-failure (System/currentTimeMillis)))
            (throw e)))))))

;; Usage
(def breaker (circuit-breaker 5 30000))  ; 5 failures, 30s reset

(defn safe-call []
  (breaker #(risky-operation)))
```
What is clojure.spec and how do I define specs?

clojure.spec is a library for describing the structure of data and functions. It provides validation, generative testing, and documentation.

**Setup**
```clojure
;; Built into Clojure 1.9+
(require '[clojure.spec.alpha :as s]
         '[clojure.spec.gen.alpha :as gen]
         '[clojure.spec.test.alpha :as stest])
```

**Basic Specs**
```clojure
;; Spec for predicates
(s/def ::name string?)
(s/def ::age pos-int?)
(s/def ::email (s/and string? #(re-matches #".+@.+\..+" %)))

;; Validate
(s/valid? ::name "Alice")  ; => true
(s/valid? ::name 123)      ; => false
(s/valid? ::age 25)        ; => true
(s/valid? ::age -5)        ; => false

;; Explain failures
(s/explain ::age -5)
;; -5 - failed: pos-int? spec: :user/age

;; explain-data returns data
(s/explain-data ::age -5)
;; => {:clojure.spec.alpha/problems [...] :clojure.spec.alpha/value -5}
```

**Composing Specs**
```clojure
;; s/and - all must pass
(s/def ::positive-even (s/and int? even? pos?))
(s/valid? ::positive-even 4)   ; => true
(s/valid? ::positive-even -2)  ; => false (not positive)
(s/valid? ::positive-even 3)   ; => false (not even)

;; s/or - any can pass (must be labeled)
(s/def ::name-or-id (s/or :name string? :id pos-int?))
(s/valid? ::name-or-id "Alice")  ; => true
(s/valid? ::name-or-id 123)      ; => true
(s/conform ::name-or-id "Alice") ; => [:name "Alice"]
(s/conform ::name-or-id 123)     ; => [:id 123]

;; s/nilable - allows nil
(s/def ::optional-name (s/nilable string?))
(s/valid? ::optional-name nil)     ; => true
(s/valid? ::optional-name "Alice") ; => true
```

**Collection Specs**
```clojure
;; s/coll-of - collection of items
(s/def ::names (s/coll-of string?))
(s/valid? ::names ["Alice" "Bob"])  ; => true
(s/valid? ::names #{"Alice" "Bob"}) ; => true

;; With options
(s/def ::name-list (s/coll-of string? :kind vector? :min-count 1 :max-count 10))
(s/valid? ::name-list ["Alice"])    ; => true
(s/valid? ::name-list [])           ; => false (min-count 1)
(s/valid? ::name-list #{"Alice"})   ; => false (not vector)

;; s/map-of - map with key and value specs
(s/def ::scores (s/map-of string? int?))
(s/valid? ::scores {"Alice" 95 "Bob" 87})  ; => true

;; s/tuple - fixed-size ordered collection
(s/def ::point (s/tuple double? double?))
(s/valid? ::point [1.0 2.0])  ; => true
(s/valid? ::point [1.0])      ; => false (wrong size)
```

**Map Specs (s/keys)**
```clojure
;; Define specs for keys
(s/def ::id pos-int?)
(s/def ::name string?)
(s/def ::email string?)
(s/def ::age pos-int?)

;; s/keys - map with required/optional keys
(s/def ::user
  (s/keys :req [::id ::name]      ; Required (namespaced)
          :opt [::email ::age]))  ; Optional

(s/valid? ::user {::id 1 ::name "Alice"})              ; => true
(s/valid? ::user {::id 1 ::name "Alice" ::age 30})    ; => true
(s/valid? ::user {::id 1})                             ; => false (missing ::name)

;; :req-un/:opt-un for unqualified keys
(s/def ::person
  (s/keys :req-un [::id ::name]   ; Unqualified keys in map
          :opt-un [::email]))     ; But still use namespaced specs

(s/valid? ::person {:id 1 :name "Alice"})  ; => true
```

**Multi-spec (Polymorphic)**
```clojure
;; Different specs based on a dispatch key
(defmulti event-type :type)
(defmethod event-type :user/created [_]
  (s/keys :req-un [::type ::user-id ::name]))
(defmethod event-type :user/deleted [_]
  (s/keys :req-un [::type ::user-id]))
(defmethod event-type :order/placed [_]
  (s/keys :req-un [::type ::order-id ::items]))

(s/def ::event (s/multi-spec event-type :type))

(s/valid? ::event {:type :user/created :user-id 1 :name "Alice"})  ; => true
(s/valid? ::event {:type :user/deleted :user-id 1})                 ; => true
(s/valid? ::event {:type :user/created :user-id 1})                 ; => false (missing :name)
```

**Conforming Data**
```clojure
;; s/conform transforms data according to spec
(s/def ::tagged (s/or :num number? :str string?))

(s/conform ::tagged 42)     ; => [:num 42]
(s/conform ::tagged "hi")   ; => [:str "hi"]
(s/conform ::tagged :kw)    ; => :clojure.spec.alpha/invalid

;; Check for invalid
(let [result (s/conform ::tagged :kw)]
  (if (= result ::s/invalid)
    (println "Invalid!")
    (println "Result:" result)))
```

**Regular Expression Specs (Sequences)**
```clojure
;; s/cat - named sequence elements
(s/def ::args (s/cat :name string? :age int? :email string?))
(s/valid? ::args ["Alice" 30 "alice@example.com"])  ; => true
(s/conform ::args ["Alice" 30 "alice@example.com"])
;; => {:name "Alice" :age 30 :email "alice@example.com"}

;; s/* - zero or more
(s/def ::strings (s/* string?))
(s/valid? ::strings [])               ; => true
(s/valid? ::strings ["a" "b" "c"])    ; => true

;; s/+ - one or more
(s/def ::at-least-one (s/+ string?))
(s/valid? ::at-least-one [])          ; => false
(s/valid? ::at-least-one ["a"])       ; => true

;; s/? - zero or one
(s/def ::optional-string (s/? string?))
(s/valid? ::optional-string [])       ; => true
(s/valid? ::optional-string ["a"])    ; => true
(s/valid? ::optional-string ["a" "b"]); => false

;; s/alt - alternatives in sequence
(s/def ::cmd (s/cat :op (s/alt :add #{:add} :remove #{:remove})
                    :target string?))
(s/conform ::cmd [:add "item"])    ; => {:op [:add :add] :target "item"}
```
How do I spec functions with clojure.spec?

clojure.spec can describe function arguments, return values, and the relationship between them.

**Basic Function Spec**
```clojure
(require '[clojure.spec.alpha :as s]
         '[clojure.spec.test.alpha :as stest])

;; Define the function
(defn add [a b]
  (+ a b))

;; Spec the function
(s/fdef add
  :args (s/cat :a number? :b number?)  ; Arguments
  :ret number?)                         ; Return value

;; Check against spec (returns problems or nil)
(s/explain (s/get-spec `add) {:args [1 2] :ret 3})
```

**Complete Function Spec**
```clojure
(defn substring
  "Returns substring from start to end"
  [s start end]
  (subs s start end))

(s/fdef substring
  :args (s/and (s/cat :s string?
                      :start nat-int?
                      :end nat-int?)
               ;; Additional validation: start <= end <= length
               (fn [{:keys [s start end]}]
                 (and (<= start end)
                      (<= end (count s)))))
  :ret string?
  :fn (fn [{:keys [args ret]}]  ; Relationship between args and return
        (= (count ret) (- (:end args) (:start args)))))

;; Test it
(stest/check `substring)
```

**:fn for Arg/Return Relationship**
```clojure
(defn reverse-string [s]
  (apply str (reverse s)))

(s/fdef reverse-string
  :args (s/cat :s string?)
  :ret string?
  :fn (fn [{:keys [args ret]}]
        (and (= (count (:s args)) (count ret))
             (= (:s args) (apply str (reverse ret))))))

;; Division with remainder
(defn div-rem [dividend divisor]
  {:quotient (quot dividend divisor)
   :remainder (rem dividend divisor)})

(s/fdef div-rem
  :args (s/and (s/cat :dividend int? :divisor int?)
               #(not (zero? (:divisor %))))
  :ret (s/keys :req-un [::quotient ::remainder])
  :fn (fn [{:keys [args ret]}]
        (= (:dividend args)
           (+ (* (:divisor args) (:quotient ret))
              (:remainder ret)))))
```

**Instrumentation**
```clojure
;; Instrument functions to check args at runtime
(stest/instrument `add)  ; Now validates args on every call

(add 1 2)      ; => 3 (valid)
(add "a" "b")  ; Throws spec error!

;; Instrument all spec'd functions
(stest/instrument)  ; All functions with fdef

;; Unstrument
(stest/unstrument `add)
(stest/unstrument)  ; All
```

**Generative Testing**
```clojure
(require '[clojure.spec.gen.alpha :as gen])

;; stest/check generates random inputs and tests function
(stest/check `add)
;; Runs 1000 tests with random inputs
;; Returns {:spec ..., :clojure.spec.test.check/ret {:result true, ...}}

;; With options
(stest/check `add {:clojure.spec.test.check/opts {:num-tests 100}})

;; Check specific functions
(stest/check [`add `substring `reverse-string])

;; Check all in namespace
(stest/check (stest/enumerate-namespace 'my.namespace))

;; Summarize results
(-> (stest/check `add) stest/summarize-results)
;; => {:total 1, :check-passed 1}
```

```clojure
;; => ("" "K" "vC" "4d" "M5p9")

                          (gen/such-that not-empty (gen/string-alphanumeric))
```

How do I use spec for data validation and transformation?

Spec is excellent for runtime data validation, especially at system boundaries (APIs, databases, etc.).

**Validation Patterns**
```clojure
(require '[clojure.spec.alpha :as s])

;; Define specs
(s/def ::id pos-int?)
(s/def ::name (s/and string? #(<= 1 (count %) 100)))
(s/def ::email (s/and string? #(re-matches #".+@.+\..+" %)))
(s/def ::age (s/and int? #(<= 0 % 150)))

(s/def ::user
  (s/keys :req-un [::id ::name ::email]
          :opt-un [::age]))

;; Simple validation
(defn valid-user? [user]
  (s/valid? ::user user))

;; Validation with error messages
(defn validate-user [user]
  (if (s/valid? ::user user)
    {:valid true :data user}
    {:valid false 
     :errors (s/explain-str ::user user)}))

;; Throw on invalid
(defn validate-user! [user]
  (if (s/valid? ::user user)
    user
    (throw (ex-info "Invalid user" 
                    {:errors (s/explain-data ::user user)
                     :data user}))))
```

**Conforming and Unforming**
```clojure
;; Conform transforms valid data
(s/def ::status (s/or :active #{"active" :active}
                      :inactive #{"inactive" :inactive}))

(s/conform ::status "active")   ; => [:active "active"]
(s/conform ::status :inactive)  ; => [:inactive :inactive]

;; Unform reverses conform
(s/unform ::status [:active "active"])  ; => "active"

;; Useful for parsing
(defn parse-status [s]
  (let [conformed (s/conform ::status s)]
    (if (= conformed ::s/invalid)
      (throw (ex-info "Invalid status" {:input s}))
      (first conformed))))  ; Get the tag: :active or :inactive

(parse-status "active")  ; => :active
```

```clojure
         '[spec-tools.spec :as spec])

;; Coercing specs

;; Coerce string to int

;; Coerce JSON-like data
```
